title: Time-bounded complementation
statement: Let $L$ be a language of finite Boolean words, let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, and let $T:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. If $M$ decides $L$ on every input of length $n$ within $T(n)$ steps, then there exist a finite Boolean-alphabet Turing machine $M'$ and natural numbers $c,a$ such that $M'$ decides the complement of $L$ within $c\bigl(T(n)+a(T(n)+1)+1\bigr)$ steps on every input of length $n$.
hypotheses_covered: $L$ is a language of finite Boolean words
$M$ is a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
